summary: Narimoto Tamayama (1916–2004) worked in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He served as a professor at Taisho University, with posts attested in 1974 and 1988.

Natalie Depraz is a philosopher who studied at the ENS de lettres et sciences humaines, Paris Nanterre University, and St. Sergius Institute. She held posts at the Collège international de philosophie, Paris-Sorbonne University, and the University of Rouen-Normandy.
Natalie Gummer is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She held a post at Harvard University attested in 2001 and became professor of religious studies at Beloit College in 2001.

Natalie Maxwell is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Stephan Beyer, and also studied under Geshe Wangyal, Khensur Ngawang Lekden, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, and Minoru Kiyota.
Natalie Rothman is a historian who studied at the University of Michigan from 1999 to 2006. She joined the University of Toronto in 2006 and taught Matthew King.

Natasha Heller is a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD from Harvard University in 2005. She was a postdoctoral fellow at UC Berkeley in 2008, taught Yu-Chen Tsui, and served at UCLA in 2016.

Natasha Reichle works in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her dissertation at the University of California, Berkeley, where she was supervised by Joanna Gottfried Williams and studied under several other scholars.
Natasja Bosma is an Indologist who completed her PhD at the University of Groningen between circa 2008 and 2018, supervised by Hans T. Bakker.

Nathan Sivin (1931–2022) was a scholar of Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at MIT, the Defense Language Institute, and Harvard, and held positions at MIT, the University of Pennsylvania, and the Chinese Academy of Sciences.

Nathan W. Hill is a Tibetologist and linguist who studied at Harvard under Leonard van der Kuijp and Jay Jasanoff. He served as reader at SOAS University of London and joined Trinity College Dublin in 2021.
Nathaniel Brassey Halhed (1751–1830) was a scholar of Indology and linguistics who studied at Harrow School and worked as an official for the East India Company from circa 1771 to 1785.
Nathaniel DeWitt Garson is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and also studied under Khenpo Namdrol.

Nathmal Tatia (1916–2002) worked in Indology, philosophy, and religious studies. He earned a Doctor of Literature at the University of Calcutta under Satkari Mookerjee and Sukhlal Sanghvi, and served as Director of the Jain Vishva Bharati Institute.
Navina Lamminger is a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned her PhD at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich under doctoral supervisor Franz-Karl Ehrhard.

Nawang Tsering Shakspo is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under doctoral supervisor Lal Mani Joshi. In 1985, he is attested as a lecturer at the Central Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Neal Arvid Donner is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who studied at the University of British Columbia, where he was a student of Leon Hurvitz.
Ng-Fung Yuen is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of the West under doctoral supervisor Kottegoda S. Warnasuriya, attested in 2009.
Ngan-che Chan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Hong Kong under Jing Yin, attested in 2007, and also studied under K. L. Dhammajoti.

Ngawang Jinpa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied at Drepung Loseling Monastery. He taught Kevin A. Vose and Samdhong Rinpoche and was a professor at St. Joseph's College, Darjeeling, attested in 1995.
Ngawang Jorden is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who taught Constance E. Kassor. He held posts at Sakya College and served as director of the International Buddhist Academy.
